name: GlassActionSheet
material_impl: Shared primitive OptimizedGlass (elevation level4) for the action group and cancel group; backdrop is raw Tailwind bg-black/40 -> bg-black/0; liquid branch delegates to LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet. Hard-coded text-red-500 / text-blue-500 for destructive/primary variants instead of tokens. Several raw Tailwind classes (translate-y-full, bg-black/40, text-blue-500) are not defined in shipped src/styles CSS.
motion: CSS transitions keyed off isAnimating set via setTimeout(10ms); exit uses setTimeout(animationDuration). Slide/fade relies on Tailwind classes translate-y-full/translate-y-0/bg-black/40 that are absent from the shipped CSS, so the entrance animation only works if the consumer runs Tailwind. No reduced-motion handling. Swipe-to-dismiss writes style.transform directly with no spring back animation.
a11y: role=dialog + aria-modal on inner panel, but no focus trap, no initial focus, no focus restore. Hard-coded ids 'action-sheet-title'/'action-sheet-message' collide when two sheets mount. Escape handled globally. Buttons get glass-focus + glass-touch-target. Backdrop is role=presentation (fine). Liquid branch buttons have no focus/touch-target classes.
api: forwardRef but the ref lands on the inner OptimizedGlass while ...props (and className) land on the wrapper div — split targets. open/onClose (not onOpenChange) — inconsistent with GlassBottomSheet/GlassDialog. Rules-of-hooks violation: early return for material='liquid' (line 120) precedes useEffect/useCallback (lines 160-225); toggling material at runtime crashes React. Keys use array index.
ssr: 'use client'. createPortal(content, document.body) at render time is guarded only by isVisible (false on first render), so SSR-safe in practice. body.style.overflow lock without restoring previous value.
fake_complexity: None claimed; sourceTransition/sourceId props are forwarded to LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet where they only become a data attribute (no real source transition).
target: Single GlassSheet (side=bottom) built on primitives/portal + FocusScope + DismissableLayer, with an 'actions' preset
justification: An iOS-style action sheet is a legitimate pattern, but this is one of at least five independent bottom-sheet implementations in the library. It has a rules-of-hooks bug on the liquid path, no focus management, colliding static ids, and its animation depends on Tailwind classes the package does not ship. The behavior should become a preset of one canonical sheet that owns portal, focus, dismissal and motion.
evidence: src/components/mobile/GlassActionSheet.tsx:256-261 (props on wrapper, ref on inner OptimizedGlass)
Pixel stats desktop.png: mean RGB 241/244/247, max chroma 20 -> fully achromatic grey-on-white render; destructive/primary colors did not render

name: GlassPullToRefresh
material_impl: OptimizedGlass for the indicator pill; no bespoke rgba. Fixed 60px offsets hard-coded.
motion: Inline CSS transitions (0.3s ease-out) and damped pull distance; glass-animate-spin spinner. No reduced-motion handling (spinner and translate transitions always run).
a11y: No aria-live/role=status for 'Refreshing...' text, no aria-busy on the scroll container, no keyboard/button alternative for triggering refresh. Indicator text is visible but not announced.
api: forwardRef to outer div, className/props passthrough. Controlled 'refreshing' mirrored into internal state (fine). onRefresh errors are swallowed silently (line 217). Native listeners re-bound on every pullDistance change because handleTouchEnd depends on pullDistance.
ssr: 'use client'; listeners attached in effect only. SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: None — it does what it says.
justification: Functionally honest and reasonably small. It needs an announced status region, aria-busy, reduced-motion handling, a ref-based pull distance so listeners stop re-binding every frame, and surfaced error state. Only one story exists and it cannot show the pulled state, so the visual is unproven.
evidence: src/components/mobile/GlassPullToRefresh.tsx:207-235 (handleTouchEnd depends on pullDistance -> effect re-binds listeners at 237-254)

name: TouchOptimizedGlass (alias TouchGlassOptimization)
material_impl: Calls createGlassStyle(level2) and then immediately overrides background/border/boxShadow with a hard-coded channelBalancedGlassStyle (rgba(255,255,255,0.28)/rgba(32,32,32,0.14)), so the shared token output is discarded. glassIntensity light/medium/heavy all map to the identical createGlassStyle call. Border radius hard-coded at 12px.
motion: framer-motion scale motion values + ripple AnimatePresence. Reduced motion is checked, but in the wrong place: animate={} with initial scale 0 means ripples never animate (harmless) while the press overlay never appears.
a11y: No role, no tabIndex, no keyboard activation for onTap/onLongPress; pure touch API. touch-none + select-none on the root blocks native scrolling. Haptics via navigator.vibrate without user opt-in.
api: forwardRef with a manual ref merge. e.preventDefault() in onTouchStart suppresses synthetic click and scrolling for children. onTap fires even after a swipe or pan (no movement threshold). The TouchGlassOptimization alias is not exported from root (only TouchOptimizedGlass is). Long-press timer is stored in state (stale closure risk).
ssr: 'use client'; window checks are guarded. SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: 'glassIntensity' and 'Optimization' are fake: the three intensities are identical and nothing is optimized.
justification: A touch-only surface that blocks scrolling and clicks, has no keyboard path, and whose intensity API does nothing. Ripple and press feedback belong in a shared interaction hook that every pressable glass control uses, not in a wrapper component.

name: MobileGlassNavigation
material_impl: Same createGlassStyle + hard-coded channelBalancedGlassStyle override; radius 24.
motion: framer drag='x' with dragConstraints 0 plus a ±50px nudge animation after a swipe; reduced motion sets duration 0.
a11y: Not navigation: no nav landmark, no keyboard equivalents for onSwipe*. drag='x' means vertical swipe detection only works from velocity.
api: Plain function (no forwardRef), className only, no style/props passthrough.
ssr: SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: Named 'Navigation' but it is a swipe-detecting div.
justification: A misnamed swipe wrapper with no navigation semantics and no keyboard path. It should be a hook if the behavior is kept at all.

name: AdaptiveGlassDensity
material_impl: Computes a density of light/medium/heavy from width and DPR, then maps all three to the identical createGlassStyle({level2}) and overrides that with the hard-coded rgba style.
motion: initial opacity 0, animate={} when reduced motion -> the content stays invisible (opacity 0) for reduced-motion users.
a11y: Content is invisible to sighted reduced-motion users.
api: Plain function, className only.
ssr: window access only in effect; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: Entirely fake: the 'adaptive density' computation has no visual effect.
justification: It does nothing it claims, and it hides content from reduced-motion users. Remove it.

name: TouchRippleEffects
material_impl: No glass; ripple color defaults to var(--glass-bg-hover). Uses raw Tailwind 'relative overflow-hidden' via template string instead of cn.
motion: framer ripple; under reduced motion ripples are mounted at scale 0 (invisible), which is acceptable.
a11y: Touch-only; no pointer or mouse support for desktop.
api: Plain function, className only. Ripple id uses Date.now(), so two touches in the same ms collide.
ssr: SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: None.
justification: This is the same ripple implemented a second time in the same file. Fold it into one pointer-event ripple hook.

name: MobileGlassBottomSheet
material_impl: createGlassStyle + hard-coded rgba override; backdrop hard-coded rgba(32,32,32,0.32).
motion: framer slide. Under reduced motion initial y:'100%' with animate={} means the sheet never comes on screen, and the backdrop stays at opacity 0 but still captures clicks.
a11y: No role=dialog, no aria-modal, no label, no focus trap, no Escape. The handle is a decorative div.
api: Plain function, isOpen (a third naming convention). Snap-point math compares a pixel Y coordinate to parseFloat('25vh')=25, so snapping is wrong. drag='y' with constraints 0/0.
ssr: SSR-safe; not portaled.
fake_complexity: snapPoints are advertised, but the math is broken.
justification: This is the fifth bottom sheet. It is invisible for reduced-motion users, has no dialog semantics, and its snap points are broken.

name: GlassBottomSheet
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level3 for the glass path; LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet for material='liquid'. Backdrop uses glass-surface-dark/50 and glass-z-1100; glass-z-1100 has no definition in src/styles, so the backdrop has no z-index.
motion: Motion primitive presets fadeIn/slideUp. The sheet Motion is always mounted; when open=false and motion is allowed, no transform is applied (line 181 only translates when !shouldAnimate). The closed sheet therefore stays rendered at its slid-in position with pointer-events-none (verified by reading code, not executed). There is no exit animation.
a11y: createModalA11y gives role/aria; announceToScreenReader on open. No focus trap or initial focus. Escape only works when focus is inside the sheet (onKeyDown). The backdrop has no aria-hidden.
api: open/onOpenChange (good) but does not extend HTMLAttributes. Rules-of-hooks violation: useA11yId (wraps useId) is called conditionally on title/description (lines 94-97). ref goes to inner OptimizedGlass while props go to the Motion wrapper.
ssr: 'use client'; not portaled; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: sourceId/presentationMode are passed through to LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet, where they are only data attributes.
justification: The closed state appears to leave the sheet visible, hooks are called conditionally, there is no focus trap, and the z-index class does not exist. A bottom sheet is a glass-signature surface, so the concept should survive as one canonical sheet with real detents, drag, and focus management.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: mean 249, sd 9, min luminance 100 -> very low-contrast pale surface, no dark text

name: GlassDialog
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level2 with liftOnHover + hoverSheen (a dialog that lifts on hover), or LiquidGlassMaterial. Backdrop is a hard-coded double linear-gradient rgba(255,255,255,.08)/rgba(15,23,42,.20). Urgency tint is hard-coded rgba(220,38,38,.12). Uses the glass-radial-reveal and glass-text-secondary-foreground classes, which are undefined in src/styles.
motion: Motion presets scale/fade/slide/flip and useReducedMotion is honored for presets. Exit is a setTimeout delay with no exit animation.
a11y: role=dialog is placed on the full-viewport wrapper (which includes the backdrop), not on the panel. trapFocus is used with manual focus restore. Escape on document. No portal, so stacking contexts can clip it. aria-label fallback is 'Dialog'.
api: Both onOpenChange and onClose. ...props are spread twice (outer wrapper and inner glass) and className is applied twice (wrapper and surface). The DialogTrigger/DialogHeader/useDialog compound parts and six Glass*Dialog consciousness variants are not exported from root (dead surface).
ssr: 'use client'; document access only in effects; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: The 'consciousness' features (predictive, eyeTracking, adaptive biometrics, spatialAudio, achievements) are inline no-op mocks: biometrics return a constant stressLevel 0.3 and eye tracking start/stop do nothing. Even so, they run a 1s setInterval re-render while open and a 3s interval when adaptive. The 'Dialog Insights' badge renders fake urgency.
target: GlassModal -> canonical GlassDialog rebuilt on Portal/FocusScope/DismissableLayer
justification: This is a 1,059-line near-copy of GlassModal. Roughly half of it is fake consciousness telemetry that causes per-second re-renders. Its focus trap is real, but role=dialog sits on the backdrop wrapper, props and className are duplicated, it is not portaled, and the dialog surface lifts on hover. Merge it into one dialog.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: mean 200/201/205 (dimmed backdrop rendered), max chroma 83, min luminance 91 -> no true dark text

name: GlassDrawer
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (liftOnHover, hoverSheen) or LiquidGlassMaterial. The backdrop uses the same hard-coded gradient as GlassDialog. Size classes are raw Tailwind (w-96, w-[28rem], h-64, rounded-l-xl); w-96 and rounded-l-xl are not defined in shipped src/styles, so drawer width depends on the consumer's Tailwind.
motion: Motion presets slideLeft/Right/Up/Down; reduced motion is honored for presets. No exit animation (timeout only). data-time-spent={Date.now()-...} is computed during render.
a11y: No focus trap and no initial focus or restore at all, even though aria-modal is true by default. Hard-coded ids 'drawer-title'/'drawer-description' collide. role=dialog sits on the full-viewport wrapper.
api: open defaults to TRUE (GlassDialog defaults to false). Rules-of-hooks violation: usePredictiveEngine/useEyeTracking/useBiometricAdaptation/useSpatialAudio/useInteractionRecorder/useAchievements are called conditionally (lines 227-232). It imports the real advanced/* modules, which pulls a large dependency graph into every drawer.
ssr: 'use client'. Date.now() in render causes hydration mismatches when SSR-rendered open.
fake_complexity: Eye tracking is wired to nothing (the startTracking call is commented out, lines 444-446). The 'Drawer Insights' badge is fake.
justification: This is a modal drawer with no focus management, conditional hooks, colliding ids, an open=true default, and width classes the package does not ship. It also imports the advanced 'consciousness' modules for features that are stubs. Fold it into a single sheet primitive with side variants.

name: GlassHoverCard
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level3 plus stacked bespoke classes (glass-backdrop-blur-md, glass-surface-dark/20, glass-border-white/20, glass-shadow-2xl), so the material is defined twice. The arrow is a bespoke bg-white/10 rotated div clipped by clip-path.
motion: Motion fadeIn, honoring the motion-preference context.
a11y: Opens on mouseenter only: no focus, no touch, no Escape. role=tooltip is placed on a card meant to hold interactive content, and the trigger gets no aria-describedby. Every open is announced with announceToScreenReader.
api: forwardRef to inner glass. Rules-of-hooks violation: conditional useA11yId (lines 194-197). The align prop is accepted but unused. The GlassHoverCardContent/Trigger compound parts are cosmetic (Trigger asChild only merges className and no handlers).
ssr: 'use client'; window only in handlers. Not portaled and uses glass-z-9999, which is undefined in src/styles.
fake_complexity: None, but the compound API is decorative.
justification: This is a third hand-rolled floating-position engine (alongside Popover and Tooltip) in a library that already ships Positioner, Portal and DismissableLayer primitives used by GlassDropdownMenu. It is mouse-only with the wrong role. Make it a hover-intent mode of one floating primitive.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: max chroma 23, min luminance 71

name: GlassModal
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level4 strong with glass-overlay-noise/glass-edge/glass-overlay-specular layers, or LiquidGlassMaterial (ior/thickness/tint). This is the best-layered material in the shard. The backdrop is the same hard-coded gradient. backdropBlur sm/md/lg all map to glass-backdrop-blur-md (fake scale).
motion: Motion presets; reduced motion honored. No exit animation (it unmounts immediately when open=false). 'flip' maps to scaleIn.
a11y: Best in shard: the FocusTrap primitive with onEscape, initialFocus/restoreFocus refs, role dialog|alertdialog, announced open, and body scroll lock that preserves scroll position. role and aria props sit on the surface, not the backdrop. Not portaled.
api: open defaults to TRUE and onClose is a no-op default. The open/onClose naming differs from Dialog/Popover (onOpenChange). Rules-of-hooks violation: conditional useA11yId (lines 309-312). 'contained' and 'compact' modes are useful. It re-exports GlassDialog/GlassDrawer.
ssr: 'use client'; mounted guard prevents SSR output entirely, so the modal never SSR-renders. Date.now() is used in a render-time data attribute.
fake_complexity: The same consciousness mocks as GlassDialog: constant stress 0.3 and no-op eye tracking. A predictive 'Modal Insights' badge is injected into user content.
target: Canonical GlassDialog/GlassSheet family (absorbs GlassDialog, GlassDrawer, GlassBottomSheet, GlassActionSheet, LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet, MobileGlassBottomSheet)
justification: This is the most correct overlay in the shard (real FocusTrap, focus restore, scroll lock, alertdialog support) and the richest material stack, so it is the right base for a flagship dialog. It still needs to drop the consciousness mocks, call hooks unconditionally, portal through primitives/portal, use onOpenChange with a false default, add exit animation via AnimatePresence, and make the blur scale real. It then becomes the single overlay engine for sheet and drawer variants.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: mean 203/204/208 (dimmed backdrop), max chroma 80

name: GlassPopover
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level4 plus stacked bespoke classes (bg-background/95, glass-backdrop-blur-md, border-border/20, shadow-lg, glass-lift, glass-sheen). bg-background/95 makes it nearly opaque, which defeats the glass. The 'solid' appearance is a plain div. The arrow uses bg-background, a raw Tailwind token.
motion: Motion presets. useReducedMotion is imported but never applied (getAnimationPreset ignores it, lines 433-448).
a11y: Trigger gets aria-expanded/aria-haspopup='dialog' but no aria-controls. The role=dialog with aria-label 'Popover content' sits on a full-viewport pointer-events-none wrapper, not on the panel. FocusTrap is used for click/focus triggers and Escape is handled. title/description are not wired to aria-labelledby, and the liquid branch drops title/description entirely.
api: Controlled/uncontrolled with defaultOpen (good). Trigger is cloneElement with a ref override, which clobbers the child's own ref. The same file declares a second, different GlassTooltip; its disabled early return precedes useState, a hooks-order violation.
ssr: 'use client'; not portaled; position computed in effect; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: None.
target: GlassPopover on primitives/positioning + portal + dismissable-layer (canonical floating surface for Popover/HoverCard/Tooltip/Menu)
justification: Its controlled/uncontrolled API and FocusTrap are a good base. It reimplements positioning and flip logic by hand instead of using the library's own Positioner, and it nests a near-opaque bg-background/95 inside glass. The role is on the wrong element, and it ships a conflicting second GlassTooltip. Rebuild it as the single floating primitive.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: min luminance 114 -> no text darker than mid-grey

name: GlassTooltip
material_impl: OptimizedGlass level4. The arrow is a CSS border triangle using glass-border-b-white/20 (near-invisible on light). glass-z-9999 is undefined in src/styles.
motion: Motion presets; respects the motion-preference context.
a11y: Fails WCAG 1.4.13/2.1.1: it opens on mouseenter only, with no focus/blur, no Escape, and no touch. aria-describedby is set on a wrapper div, not on the focusable trigger. Every show also triggers announceToScreenReader, which double-announces.
api: forwardRef. Position styles are computed during render from tooltipRef, which is null on the render that mounts the tooltip, so the first (and usually only) render places it at its static position and not next to the trigger. Rules-of-hooks: `id || useA11yId(...)` is a conditional hook call. GlassTooltipTrigger/GlassTooltipContent are exported from root but are pass-through fragments that do nothing.
ssr: 'use client'; not portaled; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: The compound Trigger/Content API is fake. The Storybook stories render a StaticTooltipPreview div (a hand-styled stand-in, not the component) to show the tooltip, so the certified screenshot is not the real component's bubble.
duplicates: GlassTooltip inside GlassPopover.tsx (same export name, different API)
target: GlassTooltip on primitives/positioning + portal (focus+hover, Escape, describedby on trigger)
justification: A tooltip is a foundational primitive, and this one is mouse-only, mispositioned on first paint, and paired with no-op compound parts. Its stories fake the visual with a static div. Two components share the GlassTooltip name with different APIs. Rebuild it on the shared floating primitive and delete the duplicate.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: max chroma 0, min luminance 117 -> monochrome, no legible dark text

name: LiquidGlassAdaptiveSheet
material_impl: LiquidGlassMaterial (material=liquid, variant regular|clear) + LiquidGlassScrollEdge, which is the correct primitive. It then overrides background with a hard-coded double white gradient and forces --glass-text-primary to rgb(15,23,42), so it is light-mode only. Backdrop button uses glass-bg-black/30; the root uses glass-z-1100, which is undefined in src/styles.
motion: None: no enter/exit animation and no detents, despite the 'adaptive' naming.
a11y: role=dialog, aria-modal only when interruptive, and the backdrop is a labeled 'Close sheet' button (nice). No focus trap, initial focus, restore, or scroll lock. aria-label=title rather than aria-labelledby to the h2.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes passthrough, open/onOpenChange. side bottom|left|right with a fixed w-96. Small and clean.
ssr: 'use client'; document only in effect. Not portaled.
fake_complexity: 'Adaptive' and sourceId 'source transition' are cosmetic: sourceId becomes data-source-id and nothing animates from the source (LiquidGlassSourceTransition primitive exists but is unused).
target: GlassSheet material='liquid' using LiquidGlassSourceTransition for real source morphs
justification: It uses the right primitive, but the Liquid Glass promise (adaptive detents, source morph, dark/light adaptation) is not implemented: it is a static light-only panel with hard-coded slate text and no motion. It should become the liquid material variant of the canonical sheet, which already has the focus and motion engine.

name: LiquidGlassPopoverMenu
material_impl: LiquidGlassMaterial, overridden with hard-coded white gradients and slate text vars. It injects a <style> block per instance with !important overrides on every button (light-only colors, min-height 44px).
motion: None.
a11y: role=menu/menuitem, but aria-checked on menuitem is invalid (needs menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio). No arrow-key roving focus, no typeahead, no Escape, no focus on open. Not positioned: it is not anchored to any trigger.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. Items-array API. 'Popover' in the name, but there is no trigger, positioning, or dismissal.
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: sourceId is a data attribute only.
duplicates: GlassDropdownMenu / GlassMenuPrimitive (real menu primitives with RovingFocus)
justification: The library already has a menu primitive with roving focus and positioning. This is an unanchored list of buttons with invalid ARIA and per-instance !important CSS injection. Its liquid look should be a material option on the real menu.

name: GlassCoherenceIndicator
material_impl: OptimizedGlass variant=frosted. createGlassStyle({blur,opacity}).background (a CSS value) is passed into className, which yields a garbage class. `${hsl(var(--x))}80` appends a hex alpha to an hsl() string, which is invalid CSS, so the gradient fails. Fixed 300x100 SVG.
motion: framer width animation honors shouldAnimate. realTimeMode setInterval(100ms) ignores reduced motion. The decoherence warning pulse honors reduced motion. Inline <animate> SVG particles ignore it.
a11y: The progress bar has no role=meter/progressbar or value attributes. The ⚠️ emoji is the status icon. The SVG has no title or desc. Hard-coded SVG pattern id 'grid' collides across instances.
api: forwardRef; className only (it does not extend HTMLAttributes, though it spreads ...props). coherenceLevel is copied into state on mount and never resynced, so the prop is effectively uncontrolled. No displayName.
ssr: Math.random() in render (decoherence circles) causes hydration mismatches. Nested components (WaveVisualization/PhaseIndicator) are defined inside render and remount every tick.
fake_complexity: The 'real-time coherence' is Math.random noise plus exponential decay. It does not measure anything.
target: Move to @aura-glass/labs (or remove); use GlassGauge/GlassProgress for real metrics
justification: This is a themed random-number widget with no product use case in a premium design system. It has invalid CSS color math, a style object passed as a className, render-time randomness, a non-reactive main prop, and no meter semantics. Eighteen stories inflate coverage for a novelty.

name: GlassProbabilityCloud
material_impl: OptimizedGlass frosted shell. Canvas colors are hard-coded rgba purple/blue. createGlassStyle({variant}) returns an object that is interpolated into a className template string ('[object Object]'). Fixed 600x400 canvas with no responsive scaling.
motion: A setInterval at 16ms updates React state unconditionally (even when realTimeMode=false and under reduced motion), re-rendering the whole component at about 60fps. The measurement ping honors reduced motion.
a11y: Canvas has no accessible name or text alternative. Emoji-only button labels (👁️ Observe). Interaction is click/hover on canvas only, so it is keyboard-inaccessible.
api: forwardRef, className string concatenation. No displayName.
ssr: 'use client'; canvas in effects; SSR-safe output, but it is CPU-heavy.
fake_complexity: Pseudo-physics on random noise. Default probabilityPoints=[] is a new array each render, so the init effect re-randomizes all particles on every 16ms render. The realTimeMode interval (50ms) depends on quantumTime, so it is torn down every 16ms before it fires and real-time mode never runs. A full-canvas createImageData is allocated each frame.
justification: It is broken by construction: a 60fps React re-render loop re-randomizes particles every tick, the advertised realTimeMode can never fire, it is not responsive, and it is inaccessible. It has no place in a production design system.

name: GlassQuantumField
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell plus bespoke glass-backdrop-blur-md/border-border/20. The canvas has class bg-black but is painted rgba(255,255,255,.18), which is contradictory. Inline style width/height fixed (default 800x600) with no responsive scaling.
motion: A rAF loop does 3-4 setState calls per frame. Because 'render' depends on particles, the effect re-subscribes every frame. Field update is O(nodes x particles) per frame (about 1200x50 at defaults). Reduced motion stops the loop (good). The measurement plays a sound via useGlassSound.
a11y: The control panel is fake: select, ranges and checkboxes all have onChange={() => {}}, so they render as controlled inputs that ignore user input. The canvas has no text alternative. Static ids (quantum-type-select etc.) collide.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. Particle uncertainty is mutated in place inside setState. Many physics props.
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe output, CPU-heavy client.
fake_complexity: The 'Schrödinger approximation'/'Heisenberg' labels decorate random motion. The controls are visually present but non-functional. The single story hides them (showControls:false, timeEvolution:false, 280x210) so the certification screenshot looks static and tidy.
justification: Its controls ignore input, its render loop costs O(n*m) per frame and re-subscribes every frame, and it is a fixed-size canvas with no semantics. The story is tuned to hide all of this. Remove it from the core package.

name: GlassQuantumTunnel
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell, but every inner surface uses a bespoke neutralGlassStyle object with hard-coded rgba gradients and backdropFilter blur(24px) saturate(1.5): a duplicated material with no tokens. Injects a <style> block with a media query per instance. Uses glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-90/60 classes, which are undefined in src/styles.
motion: setInterval-driven state updates, framer overlays; reduced motion is partially honored. The canvas is 800x300 scaled via CSS (good responsive fallback with a mobile state rail).
a11y: role=region with label. Desktop state overlays are clickable motion.divs (not keyboard reachable). The mobile rail uses real buttons (better). Canvas has no text alternative.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. Default quantumStates=[] is a new array each render, and the init effect calls setQuantumParticles([]) with a new array each time, so rendering without quantumStates loops forever (code-read, not executed).
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe output.
fake_complexity: Random 'tunneling events'. 'Wave Coherence' is just cos(time).
justification: This is a decorative pseudo-physics demo with a bespoke duplicated material, undefined utility classes, per-instance style injection, and a likely infinite render loop at default props. It has no product role.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: max chroma 21 -> grey-on-white

name: GlassSuperpositionalMenu
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell overridden by an inline backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,.3). Every card and button uses the bespoke menuGlassStyle object (same blur(24px) saturate(1.5) rgba recipe as the Tunnel, copy-pasted).
motion: A 16ms setInterval updates quantumTime forever (even under reduced motion). The QuantumState/WaveFunction/QuantumNoise/EntanglementLines components are defined inside render, so every 16ms tick unmounts and remounts every menu item, destroying framer state, hover, and focus.
a11y: role=menu, but items are non-focusable motion.divs with onClick (no menuitem role, no tabIndex, no keyboard). Action buttons have a nonsensical aria-expanded='true'. Emoji labels (🔬, ⚛, 🔄).
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. The 'Entangle' button calls currentStates.sort(), mutating state in place. menuStates is copied to state once and never resynced.
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe output.
fake_complexity: A menu whose items randomly change probability and must be 'measured' to select: an anti-usability gimmick.
justification: It is an inaccessible menu that remounts its items 60 times per second and whose selection model is deliberately random. It contradicts what a design system menu is for.

name: GlassWaveFunction
material_impl: OptimizedGlass frosted shell. createGlassStyle(...).background is passed into className (a garbage class). Canvas strokeStyle is assigned CSS variables ('var(--glass-bg-default)', 'var(--glass-white)'), which canvas cannot resolve, so the assignments are ignored and the grid and interference lines draw in whatever color was set last. A Tailwind arbitrary class is built from a template string (glass-duration-[150ms]), which cannot be compiled. Fixed 800x400 canvas.
motion: A rAF loop gated on realTimeMode && shouldAnimate (the best-behaved in the folder). Wave rows use framer whileHover/whileTap without reduced-motion gating.
a11y: Wave rows are clickable motion.divs with no keyboard or role. Canvas has no text alternative. Amplitude labels are positioned with magic margins.
api: forwardRef, className. No displayName. Props do not extend HTMLAttributes, though ...props is spread.
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: Low: it plots real sine and gaussian functions from the given equations. The 'phase space' and 'spectrum' are crude approximations.
target: Move to labs; a real need is covered by the chart family
justification: This is the least broken quantum component (honest plotting, motion-aware rAF), but it is still a fixed-size canvas demo with CSS variables that canvas ignores, and it does not belong in core. Deprecate it into a labs/demo package.

name: QuantumEntanglementVisualizer
material_impl: OptimizedGlass, with raw Tailwind bg-gradient-to-br from-white/10 via-purple-500/15 and per-state emerald/amber/rose Tailwind classes plus backdrop-blur on inner cards. These raw Tailwind classes are not in shipped src/styles. Uses undefined glass-text-primary-opacity-70 classes. glass-gradient-primary is repeated three times in one className.
motion: None (a hover border transition only).
a11y: role=table on a card grid with no rows or cells, which is wrong. The progress bar has no meter semantics. A dl/dt/dd structure is used for metrics (good).
api: Plain function, no forwardRef, no style/props passthrough. Uses '@/lib/utils' cn while every sibling uses lib/utilsComprehensive. Falls back to hard-coded DEFAULT_PAIRS demo data when pairs is empty.
ssr: SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: The name says 'Visualizer', but it is a static card list of demo data. There is no visualization of entanglement.
justification: A static demo-data card with the wrong table role, unshipped Tailwind color classes, an inconsistent API, and no tests. A generic stat/metric card already covers any real need.

name: GlassRating
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (elevation level1) wrapper, optional via glass=false. Star colors are raw Tailwind text-blue-500/purple/green/yellow/red-500 classes, none of which are defined in shipped src/styles, so stars fall back to inherited text color (the screenshot is achromatic, max chroma 28). Sizes w-4..w-10 are Tailwind.
motion: CSS hover:scale-110/active:scale-95, correctly disabled under useReducedMotion.
a11y: radiogroup/radio with roving tabIndex, aria-label per star, arrow keys, Enter/Space, glass-focus and glass-touch-target. Bugs: aria-checked is true for every star <= value (a radio group must have exactly one checked); arrow keys change value but do not move DOM focus; arrow keys step whole stars even with allowHalf; aria-required defaults to true for any non-readOnly rating.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes, className/style passthrough, unique gradient ids via useId (good). Controlled-only: no defaultValue or internal state, so clicking does nothing without onChange. The custom icon only applies to filled stars and is ignored for half state.
ssr: 'use client'; SSR-safe.
fake_complexity: None.
duplicates: none found in src/components (no other Rating/StarRating)
justification: This is a solid, honest control with the best accessibility scaffolding in the shard, but it is an orphan: it is not exported from src/index.ts or any subpath, so consumers cannot import it. Before export it needs: token-based star colors (the Tailwind color classes do not ship, so stars render grey), single aria-checked, focus that follows arrow keys, half-step keyboard support, and uncontrolled defaultValue support.
evidence: src/index.ts (no GlassRating export; rg finds no reference outside src/components/rating)
